extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, agents, and attorneys)
extracted.subtask_short: examiner's answer in ex parte appeal
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparation, content, timing, and consequences of an examiner's answer in appeals and ex parte reexamination proceedings (MPEP §2275). Covers incorporation of rejections, new grounds, appellant response options, timing, remands, and panel review requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for furnishing examiner's answer
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary examiner may, within such time as may be directed by the Director, furnish a written answer to the appeal brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner's answer must be furnished within the time directed by the Director; timing interacts with remand and Board jurisdiction rules described elsewhere in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of grounds of rejection in examiner's answer
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner's answer is deemed to incorporate all of the grounds of rejection set forth in the Office action from which the appeal is taken (as modified by any advisory action and pre-appeal brief conference decision), unless the examiner's answer expressly indicates that a ground of rejection has been withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner intends to remove any previously stated ground of rejection, the examiner must expressly indicate that the ground has been withdrawn in the examiner's answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: New ground of rejection designation and approval
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner's answer may include a new ground of rejection. For purposes of the examiner's answer, any rejection that relies upon any Evidence not relied upon in the Office action from which the appeal is taken (as modified by any advisory action) shall be designated by the primary examiner as a new ground of rejection. The examiner must obtain the approval of the Director to furnish an answer that includes a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any ground that depends on evidence newly relied upon (not in the underlying Office action) must be labeled a new ground and Director approval is required before including it in the examiner's answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant option — reopen prosecution (response to new ground)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner’s answer contains a rejection designated as a new ground of rejection, appellant must within two months from the date of the examiner’s answer exercise one option: Reopen prosecution. Request that prosecution be reopened before the primary examiner by filing a reply under §1.111 of this title with or without amendment or submission of affidavits (§§1.130, 1.131 or 1.132 of this title) or other Evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment or submission of affidavits or other Evidence must be relevant to the new ground of rejection. A request that complies will be entered and the application or the patent under ex parte reexamination will be reconsidered by the examiner under §1.112. Any request that prosecution be reopened will be treated as a request to withdraw the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant option — maintain appeal (reply brief restrictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner’s answer contains a rejection designated as a new ground of rejection, appellant may instead maintain the appeal by filing a reply brief as set forth in §41.41. Such a reply brief must address as set forth in §41.37(c)(1)(iv) each new ground of rejection and should follow the other requirements of a brief as set forth in §41.37(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reply brief may not be accompanied by any amendment, affidavit (§§1.130, 1.131 or 1.132) or other Evidence. If a reply brief filed pursuant to this section is accompanied by any amendment, affidavit or other Evidence, it shall be treated as a request that prosecution be reopened under paragraph (b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits and extensions for replying to examiner's answer
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant must, within two months from the date of the examiner's answer, elect either to reopen prosecution or to maintain the appeal; Extensions of time under §1.136(a) of this title for patent applications are not applicable to the time period set forth in this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For extensions of time to reply, see §1.136(b) for patent applications and §1.550(c) for ex parte reexamination proceedings; do not rely on §1.136(a) for the two-month period specified in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of MPEP §1207–§1207.05 and reexamination differences
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP §1207 through §1207.05 relate to preparation of examiner’s answers in appeals. The procedures covered in these sections apply to appeals in both patent applications and patents undergoing ex parte reexamination proceedings, except as provided for in this Chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable exception: there is no requirement for pre-appeal conferences in reexamination proceedings but there is a requirement for panel review of the examiner’s answer in reexamination proceedings. See the referenced MPEP sections for preparation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board jurisdiction after reply brief or expiration of reply time
rubrics_metrics.description: After receipt of a reply brief in compliance with 37 CFR 41.41 or the expiration of the time in which to file such a reply brief (37 CFR 41.35), jurisdiction over the appeal passes to the Board. Normally, the examiner does not need to acknowledge the reply brief and will not have an opportunity for further comment prior to a decision by the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once jurisdiction passes to the Board, the examiner typically has no further role unless the Board remands the case; parties should expect Board handling thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand and substitute examiner's answer conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may remand the appeal to the examiner to furnish a substitute examiner’s answer responsive to the remand or the Director may remand the proceeding under 37 CFR 41.35(c), such as where there has been a change of law that would require that a new ground of rejection be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 41.50(a)(2) and MPEP §1207.05 for information on substitute examiner’s answers. A substitute examiner’s answer is not permitted unless the reexamination proceeding has been remanded by the Board or Director for such purposes.
